subject: Re: Unexpected small/ghost requests from staging leading to usage overage
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@luminahealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: accounts-payable@luminahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Unexpected surge — tiny 'ghost' requests from staging causing overage

Hi Camila,

We flagged a weird usage spike on Nov 6–7 that pushed us over our monthly threshold. The pattern looks odd — thousands of <1-token requests (mostly 0 or 1 token billed) tied to a set of request IDs that start with "ghst-". We attached a small sample (ingest-sample-ids.csv) with timestamps and request IDs.

We suspected a client-side retry loop, but the requests appear to originate from a staging IP range we gave you for a test integration. This generated a ~$4.2k overage on our invoice.

Can you 1) pause collection or block the request pattern while we investigate, 2) provide a per-request export for Nov 6 00:00–Nov 7 23:59 (request id, path, tokens_in, tokens_out), and 3) advise next steps for a credit/refund? Our AP team is on the CC.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Director of Platform Integrations
Lumina Health

Attachment: ingest-sample-ids.csv

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@luminahealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge — tiny 'ghost' requests from staging causing overage

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample. I'm escalating immediately to our billing and platform teams to pull a scoped export and look for the "ghst-" prefix.

Next steps from my side:
- I'll ask Billing for a provisional invoice hold for the suspected window while we triage.
- Platform will run a targeted query (request_id + token counts) and paste the results here by EOD tomorrow.
- If this is confirmed as non-production/staging noise, we'll propose a one-time credit and a short remediation plan.

Can you confirm whether any internal CI/CD pipelines or Canary jobs were running Nov 6–7 that might have sent repeated health pings? Any links to the sample traces are helpful.

I'll follow up shortly.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: token-sample-request.csv

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T11:25:00-05:00
Subject: FW: Unexpected surge — tiny 'ghost' requests from staging causing overage

Internal — forwarding Lumina's sample and timeline. Key points from their CSV: ~38k requests over 48h with request IDs prefixed ghst-; tokens_in is mostly 0–2; billed tokens aggregated to ~42,300 token-units resulting in the $4.2k delta.

Quick log snippet they included:
"2026-11-06T02:13:12Z ghst-7a2b ping /v1/generate tokens_in=0 tokens_out=1 client_ip=54.23.11.45"
"2026-11-06T02:13:12Z ghst-7a2b ping /v1/generate tokens_in=0 tokens_out=1 client_ip=54.23.11.45"

This looks like a rapid-fire health check retry causing many tiny billing events rather than a single aggregated session. Ben — can Platform run a query for request_id LIKE 'ghst-%' between 2026-11-06T00:00Z and 2026-11-07T23:59Z and provide: count, unique client_ip, model used, tokens billed per-request, and which backend shard handled the requests?

If this is confirmed as staging traffic misrouting, I want to offer Lumina a one-time goodwill credit and clear them from the invoice while we fix routing. Please advise how much we can approve at AE level vs. needing finance sign-off.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: FW: Unexpected surge — tiny 'ghost' requests from staging causing overage

Camila / Marissa,

Platform findings (summary):
- Confirmed ~36,870 requests with prefix 'ghst-' in the requested window.
- 92% of those requests were <2 billed tokens; however our per-request billing counts them as individual events which aggregated to the $4,200 total.
- Traffic originated from Lumina's staging CIDR (54.23.11.0/24) and was routed to public hosted nodes due to a misconfigured environment variable in their SDK that toggled a prod endpoint for health checks. Essentially a retry loop caused many discrete requests instead of a single keepalive.

Attached is a short extract (infected-reqids.txt) with representative IDs and timestamps. Root cause appears customer-side but we should treat this as a friendly operational incident.

Recommendation:
1) Offer a one-time goodwill credit for the billed amount ($4,200) conditional on Lumina confirming the staging change and sharing the CD/CI job that caused it.
2) Refund the invoice line for Nov 6–7 once Lumina provides a signed acknowledgement that they'll patch the SDK env var and run a scoped replay in staging.
3) Apply a temporary protective rule: treat requests with the 'ghst-' prefix and client IPs from their staging CIDR as nonbillable for the disputed window (execution done by billing ops).

I think finance can approve up to $5k for goodwill credits for strategic accounts; beyond that we'd need SVP sign-off.

Ben
Billing & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: infected-reqids.txt

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@luminahealth.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@luminahealth.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge — tiny 'ghost' requests from staging causing overage

Alex — thanks for your patience. Platform and Billing have reviewed the samples and we can see the ghst-* pattern from your staging CIDR. Based on our analysis we will:

1) Place a provisional hold on the disputed invoice line for Nov 6–7 while we complete final validation.
2) Apply a one-time goodwill credit of $4,200 to the outstanding amount conditional on your team confirming the staging change (a short note from your SRE/CI owner is fine).
3) We will also apply a temporary inbound filter so future ghst-* prefixed requests from your staging CIDR in that window are not billed retroactively.

Please reply to confirm the patch will be applied; once we have that confirmation Billing will complete the refund/credit process (expect 5–10 business days for credit settlement). If you prefer a faster route we can open a support ticket and run a scoped raw-export for the exact timestamp window (I included a Drive link to upload any CI logs).

Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate Lumina's partnership and will help prevent this recurrence.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
